items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: Maxted said, “call this kid” because he had my number.

ctx.x: Well that’s a long story. You see when I left Bob Astor’s band, before I left Bob Astor’s band we were working in Youngstown, Ohio at the Elms Ballroom. And we were there for four weeks. And there was a local theater where bands used to come in and play, and what’s his name, Ray McKinley and Wilbur, the trombone player, now the age is catching me. Ray McKinley and Will Bradley, Bradley-McKinley, you know, 18th and Chestnut, between 18th and 19th on whatever, you know. Anyway, they came into town. They were…

band, and when Bradley wanted us to join his band, most of the guys with Astor’s band went with him, including me, but the thing was that Billy Maxted, when I went to the rehearsal he was playing piano and he says, “I’m not leaving the band until I get my money, because he owes me a lot of money for arrangements, see, and when I get my money I’ll call you, and you take my place.” I says okay. So in the meantime I used to go to Local 802. First we’d go to Local 802 to look for jobs, and then we would go to Nola…
And then you walked in the door.
